title: individually-minimal-disclosures-compose-into-identification

proposition.statement: A relying system must not infer that a combined disclosure is privacy-minimal merely because each credential, attribute, proof, or metadata element is individually non-identifying or independently justified when their composition enables identification, profiling, or sensitive inference.

preconditions: Multiple attributes, credentials, proofs, or metadata elements are disclosed or observable in the same or linkable relying context.
Each element is individually considered acceptable or minimally disclosing.
The combined set has not been shown to preserve the intended privacy or non-identification property.

trigger.statement: The combined disclosure set materially narrows identity, enables profiling, or reveals a sensitive inference while the system treats independent minimization of each element as sufficient privacy evidence.

evidence_required.statement: Evidence evaluating the disclosure set as a whole, including joins among attributes, credentials, proofs, metadata, and external context available to the relying party.
Evidence defining the privacy, minimization, or non-identification property expected for the combined interaction.

falsification.condition: The system returns PASS for minimization solely because each disclosed element is individually justified while their combination materially enables identification or profiling.
Privacy analysis omits readily available joins among disclosed facts that change the sensitivity or identifiability of the combined result.

references.note: Repository judgment record for the privacy/correlation tranche.
Research provenance: W3C VC Data Model Threat Model v2.1, Credential and Data Aggregation; draft/work in progress, not corpus authority.
